script:
Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Saturday, November 21. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 9 degrees Celsius, clear skies. The high will be 17 and the low 8 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 0 percent.

You have no appointments scheduled in the next 24 hours.

Now, the top 5 stories in AI today.

First, from Ars Technica: Google Redesigns Search Homepage with AI Chat History, Removes Search Button. Google is rolling out a new search homepage that integrates AI chat history directly into the search page and removes the traditional search button. The change makes AI tools more prominent and accessible on Google's main search interface, potentially shifting how billions of users interact with search and AI simultaneously. Why it matters: Represents a major interface shift at the world's dominant search engine, directly affecting how businesses and consumers access AI in daily workflows.

Second, from The Verge: Anthropic Researcher Claims Claude Helped Solve the Riemann Hypothesis. An Anthropic mathematician, Levent Alpöge, claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis with assistance from Claude, one of mathematics' most notorious unsolved problems. A competing human solution also reportedly emerged. If verified, the achievement would mark a major milestone for AI in mathematical discovery and could reshape how researchers approach Millennium Prize problems. Why it matters: A verified AI-assisted solution to a centuries-old math problem would be a seismic breakthrough for AI reasoning and enterprise R&D applications.

Third, from OpenAI: OpenAI Details Defenses Against Adversarial Distillation of AI Models. OpenAI published a layered approach to combatting adversarial distillation, combining model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction. The technique aims to prevent rivals or malicious actors from distilling proprietary model capabilities into competing systems. This addresses growing concerns about model intellectual property and competitive moats in the AI industry. Why it matters: Directly affects enterprise AI strategy, model licensing, and how companies protect proprietary AI capabilities from extraction.

Fourth, from The Verge: Signal Blocks Gemini and Siri AI from Reading User Screens. Signal is restricting screenshot capabilities on Android and iOS to prevent AI agents built into operating systems from reading users' messages and other data. Signal's president said these agentic AI capabilities, which analyze on-screen information, undermine the app's ability to guarantee privacy. The move highlights growing tension between AI agents and encrypted messaging privacy. Why it matters: Signals a critical privacy boundary for enterprise AI agents and operating system-level AI features that access screen content.

Fifth, from Ars Technica: Meta Reconsiders 2030 Net-Zero Goal Amid AI Data Center Emissions. Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero sustainability goal due to record emissions from AI data centers. The development raises questions about whether other tech companies will follow suit as AI infrastructure drives power consumption and carbon output higher. It underscores the environmental cost of scaling AI workloads. Why it matters: Highlights the growing tension between AI infrastructure expansion and corporate sustainability commitments, affecting enterprise ESG planning.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
